current.text: Experts take him first overall in head-to-head category leagues, ahead of Victor Wembanyama.
He has the tightest range of any first-round player. His best case is 1st overall and his worst case is 3rd.
In a 2026-10-05 auction mock he sold for 80 USD to the manager who also bought Wembanyama.
Josh values him at 73 to 74 USD. If the room spends evenly and he sits at 55 USD, take him: that frees about 20 USD for other players.
Experts expect about 35 minutes again and are not very worried about more regression in his threes, minutes or steals. He is projected for over 30 percent usage.
Among the assist leaders, he had the fewest potential assists. His assists could drop to about 10.1 per game if his teammates' shooting evens out.
He could become a free agent after this season.
Moore expects him to stay in Denver all season and re-sign, even though he has not been happy for two years.

Denver plays 43 games through March 28, one below the maximum. It has only 14 back-to-backs, one of the lowest counts in the league. He plays four games in the week starting March 15, which is our week 20.
Moore doubts Denver will rest Jokic, Murray or Gordon on purpose. He predicts about 50 wins.
He is healthy going into the season, and so is most of the Denver roster.

durable.text: He has been the best fantasy player of the last five or six years. He finished number one in both category and points leagues.
He is a center who gives elite rebounds and assists. These two categories rarely come together, which adds to his value.
He is a league outlier in FG% on high volume, and also in points, rebounds and assists.
Turnovers are his one clearly weak category. He projects for about 3.4 per game.
He has no significant weakness outside turnovers. Threes, blocks and free throws are only relative weaknesses, and his free throws are fine but not a strength.
He had a hamstring injury two seasons ago. Last season he had a somewhat fluky knee injury and missed significant time.
At 31 he may be getting slightly less durable, but experts are not worried.
He tires on defense in the middle of the season more than he admits.

note: He is the consensus first pick for H2H categories. Prices are rising: Yahoo values him at 61 USD (average cost 71 USD), ESPN at 68 USD (average cost 81.4 USD), a recent mock sold him for 80 USD, and he went for 87 USD in our league last season. Expect to pay 80 to 90 USD, and grab him if the room lets him drop toward 55 USD. He fits any build and fits best in punt TO, because turnovers are his only weak category. Early in the season, check that he is playing about 35 minutes and getting about 10 assists, and watch the knee that cost him games last season.
